events.title: Tesla reports nearly half a million deliveries
events.description: The company says it delivered about 500,000 vehicles in 2020. Deliveries measure activity, not profit.

what_happened_next.text:
Tesla grew to about 21 times its starting value, far ahead of the other choices. Disney and Boeing also gained overall, while the U.S. share basket more than doubled. Tesla reported delivering nearly 500,000 vehicles in 2020 and its first full-year net profit. Boeing reported a large 2020 loss as the pandemic and the 737 MAX grounding hurt deliveries. Disney opened a resort in Shanghai, then estimated that the pandemic cut operating profit in its parks, experiences and products business by $6.9 billion in 2020.

The final values followed years of very different business conditions. The pandemic arrived near the end of the holding period. In March 2020, WHO described COVID-19 as a pandemic; by December, it had listed its first COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use. These facts show why forecasts can change quickly, but they do not assign one event to one share-price result.

Tesla’s huge gain can make Disney’s and Boeing’s gains look small on the same chart, even though both finished higher. Vehicle deliveries and profit are different measures. A spectacular winner is not a reasonable promise for every exciting company. Compare the rises and falls along each path with the broad basket, and remember that investors had to decide before they knew which line would finish highest.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: New films, electric cars, aircraft orders and a possible distant planet made news. Companies announced ambitious plans.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Company shares could move very differently from broad baskets. Tesla’s huge gain also came with sharp swings that an investor would have had to endure.
reflection.what_faded_away: A record film or an aircraft sales report did not reveal the whole five-year journey. A company’s promise still had to become reality.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The pandemic and the size of Tesla’s gain were unknown. This selected winner does not mean every exciting young company would do the same.

hot:2016-01:disney.text: Shanghai Disney Resort opened in June 2016, giving Disney its first resort in mainland China. In 2020, the pandemic shut parks and limited visitors. Disney estimated that closures and reduced capacity cut operating profit in its parks, experiences and products business by $6.9 billion that year.

hot:2016-01:boeing.text: Boeing reported a net loss for 2020 as the pandemic cut air travel and the 737 MAX grounding continued to hurt deliveries. Commercial Airplanes revenue fell sharply from the year before. Airlines buy planes over many years, so grounded aircraft and fewer orders can weigh on a manufacturer well beyond one quarter.

hot:2016-01:tesla.text: Tesla reported delivering nearly 500,000 vehicles in 2020. In January 2021, it announced its first full-year net profit, $721 million. It was building cars at a much larger scale, and sales of clean-vehicle credits also helped its operating profit in the final quarter.
